title: When the Choir Falls
premise: Marguerite Oyelaran, a storm-caller exiled to a valley where magic dies, has spent years hiding among the mute villagers who took him in. When a dying courier leaves him a map and a plea, Marguerite must cross into the magic-hungry world beyond, where his voice can call storms but also mark him for death by the usurper Veyra's hunters. Along the way he gathers a ragged found family—a disgraced cartographer, a half-fae runaway, and an old rival turned reluctant ally—and learns the 'broken covenant' was shattered by his own order's betrayal, not by his exile. In the climax at the free city of Solmere, Marguerite reforges the covenant at the cost of his own storm-voice, choosing belonging over power; the armies break against the renewed wards, and he returns to the valley not as an exile but as a bridge between realms.
about_author: Coral Marchetti is the pen name of a former choir director who grew up in a coastal town where weather was a family member. She writes fantasy about outsiders who learn that home is something you build, not something you're granted.

chapters.title: The Valley That Swallows Thunder
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In the magic-dead valley, Marguerite tends bees and buries his past until a dying courier collapses at his door, pressing a bloodstained map into his hands and naming him 'the last voice of the covenant.' Hunters arrive within days. The emotional beat is the terror of losing the invisibility he hated but depended on, and the first flicker of obligation to something larger than survival.

chapters.title: Road of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, with interludes from cartographer Sefa. Crossing the border, Marguerite's suppressed magic surges back painfully; he rescues half-fae runaway Ilex from Veyra's patrols and is rescued in turn by Sefa, who recognizes the map as her stolen life's work. The emotional beat is wary trust forming among strangers, each hiding a broken identity, as they realize Veyra is hunting the covenant's heirs one by one.

chapters.title: What the Usurper Cannot Sing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Marguerite and Veyra. Captured and brought before Veyra, Marguerite learns the covenant was broken by his own mentor's betrayal—and that Veyra, once a storm-caller herself, was silenced by the same order. She offers him a place at her side. The emotional beat is the seduction of grievance; Marguerite nearly accepts before seeing the conscripted children of Solmere and choosing, trembling, to escape and finish the covenant's reforging himself.

chapters.title: When the Choir Falls
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At Solmere, with Veyra's armies at the gates, Marguerite, Sefa, and Ilex reach the covenant-stone; reforging it demands a voice surrendered forever. Marguerite sings his last storm, breaking the siege and Veyra's claim, then wakes voiceless among his found family. The emotional beat is grief transmuted into belonging: he returns to the valley not exiled, but chosen, as the bridge between two worlds.
